answer: A harbor admission system works like a trellis for young vines: a new agent starts with a tiny transaction limit and must earn trust by completing small, publicly auditable jobs whose payments sit in escrow. Each completed job lengthens its record, like quartz forming layer by layer, and raises its limit only slowly. Forging a thousand fake identities gains nothing, because each fake must separately do months of real, checkable work before it can move meaningful value, while one caught cheat forfeits its escrow and resets its whole history to zero.
